title: App Desktop and Store
summary: Find and install tools, choose a source, then apply your configuration and launch the app.
body:
Apps: keep familiar tools together

App Desktop brings together AI clients, CLIs, and related tools. Select an icon to see the accounts and model settings available for that tool on the right. You still use the client you know; EchoBird provides a central place to manage its entry point and supported settings.

Tools do not all support the same operations. Some can switch official accounts, some accept API model configurations, and others mainly provide a launch entry. Check the options actually shown for the selected tool.

An installed tool is not detected

  1. Confirm that the third-party tool has finished installing and can launch normally from your operating system.
  2. Return to EchoBird and click Refresh to scan for local tools again.
  3. If it is still missing, open the tool path settings and check the location of its executable.
  4. Correct the path and refresh again. Do not point to a launcher from another project, or overwrite an existing account configuration simply to make detection succeed.

Store: from discovery to installation

Store organizes tools that are not installed yet. Select a tool and click Get App to open AI Assistant with an installation request already filled in. Continue the installation based on the assistant’s output and your system environment.

Browsing does not install anything automatically

Browsing Store or selecting an icon does not automatically install software. Installation may involve downloads, dependencies, network access, and system permissions. When the assistant finishes, return to App Desktop, refresh detection, and actually launch the tool to verify the result.

Put an account or model to work in a tool

  1. Select an installed tool, then choose an official account or an API model. These choices are mutually exclusive, so the client does not receive conflicting identities and endpoints.
  2. Check the options at the bottom: whether to write configuration and whether to launch at the same time. If you only want to configure the tool, use the options it supports.
  3. Run the main action and wait for the result. Follow any prompts about a running client or restoring official endpoints.
  4. Open the client and verify its actual identity and model. A highlight on the right shows your current selection; it does not guarantee that every already-running window switches immediately.

Web Search, Image, and 1M

CapabilityWhat it configuresWhat to know
Web SearchWeb search settings for supported toolsAlso depends on the model and service capabilities
ImageImage input settings for supported toolsTurning it on does not give a text-only model vision capabilities
1MLarge-context mode for supported toolsActual context length, costs, and limits depend on the tool and service

The pill buttons are independent and can be enabled separately. In the real client, some tools reapply capability settings when a valid API configuration is already selected; these buttons do not always change appearance alone. If a button is absent, follow the capabilities exposed by the current tool.

A recommended approach

Keep one working official account or model configuration, then establish a clear selection routine for your usual tools. When you need multiple sources and failover, connect the tool to Smart Routes instead of repeatedly changing endpoint addresses inside each client.

title: Accounts
summary: Add and manage accounts, and understand plans, quotas, balances, and authorization status.
body:
Save an account, then decide where to use it

Accounts brings together accounts from integrated services and the usage information they provide. A service can have multiple accounts, and one page can manage accounts from different services. Use it to compare status, refresh data, and maintain authorization. Clicking an account card does not by itself switch an external client.

Add your first account

  1. Find the service in the service list and click Add Account.
  2. Complete browser sign-in, device-code authorization, client sign-in, or another supported flow as required by the service. Steps and prerequisites vary.
  3. Wait for EchoBird to save the authorization result. You can cancel while waiting. If the flow times out, start again rather than continuing to wait for the old attempt.
  4. Confirm the identity shown on the card, then go to App Desktop, select the corresponding app and account, and apply the selection or launch.

Adding a new login for some services requires their client to be installed locally. Whether an existing account can be refreshed or managed without that client also depends on its integration. Check the current entry’s guidance; you do not need to reinstall every client just to manage saved records.

Read quotas and balances correctly

Displayed informationHow to interpret it
PlanThe account’s subscription or service tier, not its remaining allowance
5-hour, weekly, or other quotasSeparate quota periods; read each percentage and reset time individually
Balance / creditsThe service’s own units, which cannot simply be added to those of other services
CountdownA time reference for the corresponding reset period or service status
— or unknownNo usable data is available yet; it means neither zero nor unlimited

Use Refresh when you need current data. Opening the page and explicitly querying a provider are different actions. Expired authorization, network problems, or a provider that does not expose a usage API can all affect the result.

Actions on account cards

  • Refresh / Refresh All: retrieve supported usage information again. This does not switch a client’s account.
  • Claim: appears only when the service offers this capability. Availability and the claim result depend on the account.
  • Warm up: applies only to integrations that provide it; not every account needs warming up.
  • Reauthorize: repeat sign-in when authorization has expired. First distinguish an authorization error from an ordinary quota-query failure.
  • Ordering and privacy: drag frequently used accounts to the front, and hide identities when sharing your screen. Hiding an identity does not remove its authorization.
  • Delete: follow the confirmation flow to remove the saved account record from EchoBird. This does not close the provider account or cancel its subscription.

A routine for working with multiple accounts

Before working, refresh your usual accounts and check the correct quota periods separately. In App Desktop, choose an account for the target tool and apply it. Prepare a separate configuration in Models if you need a backup API. Do not assume subscription allowances from multiple accounts can be pooled for all models.

title: Models
summary: Organize API addresses, keys, and model IDs, test the connection, then use the model in your tools.
body:
What the four fields mean

FieldPurposeExamples and notes
NameHelps you recognize a configurationFor example, “Everyday writing” or “Backup coding”; it need not match the model ID
Endpoint addressThe API endpoint actually provided by the serviceDistinguish OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible, and regional endpoints
API KeyA credential for calling the serviceObtain it from the provider; it is not your website sign-in password
Model IDThe model identifier accepted by the servicePrefer the model list returned by that service rather than guessing from a product nickname

Add and verify a model

  1. Open Models and choose a service from the provider or relay directory, or enter your own service through the available form.
  2. Check its region, plan, and protocol version. A company’s subscription endpoint and general API endpoint are not necessarily interchangeable.
  3. Enter the real address and key. Services that support model discovery can return candidate IDs; for other services, use the IDs in their actual documentation.
  4. Choose a recognizable name and save. Click Test Latency at the top of Config view to check the endpoint’s connection status and latency.
  5. Then select a supported tool in App Desktop and apply the configuration, or add it to a Smart Routes scheme. Send a request in the real tool or AI Assistant to verify the model’s reply.

Connection tests, replies, and usage answer different questions

Test Latency at the top of Config view checks an endpoint’s connection and latency. It is not a chat test, and cannot on its own confirm that the API Key, model ID, or reply content works correctly. To verify a model, send a request in a real tool or AI Assistant. Usage view queries the balance or quota information exposed by the service.

Actual model requests may be billed under the provider’s rules. A model that replies does not necessarily expose a balance API. Some usage queries need additional settings or authorization, and a failed query does not by itself prove the model is unusable.

Edit, reorder, and delete

Put your usual configurations first and use clear names to distinguish work, everyday, and backup sources. After editing, verify that the address, model ID, and credentials still match, then confirm that the target tool uses the configuration you intended.

Deleting a local entry does not delete the provider account or remotely revoke its API Key. Replace or revoke a key with the provider, then update the configurations that need it in EchoBird.

A common misunderstanding: saving did not change the tool

Models is a configuration library. Saving creates the entry; it does not automatically switch every external client to that model. Next, select the tool in App Desktop and apply the configuration, or reference it in Smart Routes and connect the tool to that scheme.

Compatible endpoints do not imply identical capabilities. Tool calling, image input, context length, and model parameters still require support from the tool, model, and integration adapter.

title: Smart Routes
summary: Organize model and account sources, switch models in real time, and keep one stable endpoint for your client.
body:
Smart Routes keeps model choice in your hands: the client connects to a local endpoint, while you manage the sources, model IDs, and attempt order behind it in EchoBird.

One scheme, an ordered route

The numbers in a scheme indicate priority. Requests try sources nearer the front first. If a source is rate-limited, out of quota, or temporarily unavailable, later sources are tried next. Once the cooldown ends, attempts return to priority order.

This is different from requesting several models simultaneously, and does not pool quotas from different providers. Whether a source is usable and which models it can access still depend on its own authorization, plan, and service capabilities.

Create your first scheme

  1. Open Smart Routes and choose a source from My Models, Account Access, or Free Models. Configurations already saved in Models can be referenced directly.
  2. Give the scheme a clear name and check its local port, access key, and model identifier. The port must be available; use the actual address displayed in the current interface.
  3. Place your usual model first and backup sources later. Dragging to reorder saves automatically and takes effect on the next request; it does not replace the model in the middle of an answer.
  4. Open a source’s model selector and choose an ID it can actually use. Fetch or refresh the service’s model list first if needed.
  5. In App Desktop, select a tool that supports model switching, choose this scheme, and apply the configuration.
  6. Send a real request in the tool, then check the access status and statistics to confirm that the request reached the expected source.

Free versus keyless

LabelWhat it meansWhat it does not mean
FreeThe specific model option in the directory is marked as freeEvery model from that provider is free, unlimited, or permanently available
KeylessThis endpoint does not require you to supply your own API KeyIt has no rate limits or conditions, or suits every task
Account AccessUses the model directory and authorization provided by an account integrationAny subscription account can call every provider’s models

Cards, lists, and the terminal

Cards help you inspect sources and select model IDs. Lists make it easier to reorder, enable, or pause entries. The terminal shows grouped request information. If the terminal explicitly identifies its data as illustrative, it does not mean you have already made real requests or incurred charges.

Removing a source from a scheme removes only that reference; the original model or account remains saved. After deleting a scheme, update any external tool that still points to its old address to use another working endpoint.

Use the OpenAI and Anthropic addresses

A scheme provides local OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible endpoints for different clients. Copy the address and key displayed for the current scheme. Do not guess an address from an example port, or manually change one protocol’s URL suffix into another.

Keep EchoBird running when using a local endpoint

After you fully quit EchoBird, the local endpoint is unavailable. Minimizing to the tray is different from quitting. If a tool suddenly cannot connect, first check that EchoBird is still running and that the scheme and port are correct.

The practical result: keep the endpoint, adjust the sources

For example, create an “Everyday coding” scheme for your coding tool: use a preferred model for routine tasks, another available service as backup, and suitable free sources when needed. Adjusting the models and their order centrally is more convenient than repeatedly changing endpoints in each client. Still review important outputs; failover does not guarantee that every model delivers the same quality.

title: Request Statistics
summary: Inspect calls, completion rates, failover, and response times to diagnose route problems.
body:
Where to find statistics

Open Statistics at the top of Smart Routes. View data for ranges such as today, 7 days, or 14 days, and for all schemes or one specific scheme. Make real requests from a tool first, then return to see what each metric represents.

Understand the numbers

MetricHow to read it
CallsRequests initiated by clients, not necessarily the number of upstream attempts
Completion rateCalculated from requests with recorded success or failure results
Successful failoverA request ultimately succeeded after changing upstream sources; not every attempt necessarily succeeded
Average duration and trendsHelp compare actual performance over the selected period
Source distribution and recent usageShow which sources handle requests and recent activity

Investigate unexpected results

  1. Check the selected time range and scheme first, so you are not looking for requests in the wrong scope.
  2. Inspect failed sources and failover results. A preferred source failing before a backup succeeds is different from the entire request failing.
  3. Return to Smart Routes and check the source’s model ID, enabled state, and priority.
  4. When needed, explicitly refresh status or test the service in Accounts or Models, then send another request to verify the result.

Statistics are not a bill

This page helps you understand requests that pass through the router. It is not a complete statement from every provider or an exact billing system. Missing request records do not mean the account balance is zero, and attempt counts cannot be treated directly as paid-call counts.

The statistics recording switch in Settings, local storage state, and selected scope all affect the data you can see. Before sharing statistics, you can hide account names to avoid exposing real identities.

title: AI Assistant
summary: Describe your goal and let the assistant check environments, install tools, or perform real tasks.
body:
Prepare a working model before starting

  1. Open AI Assistant. In normal conversation mode, first choose a configured model that works.
  2. Confirm whether the target is this computer or an SSH server added on the right. The target determines the context for subsequent operations.
  3. Explain what you want to do, which tool is involved, and the result you expect. Include the specific error if needed.
  4. After sending, watch the working status, tool calls, and results. Expand tool cards to inspect arguments and output.

Requests that work better than “fix this for me”

  • “Check the installation and launch environment for Claude Code on this computer, and tell me what problems you find first.”
  • “Help me install Git, then check that it is available in the terminal.”
  • “This tool reports the following error when it starts: … Please investigate the cause and explain what you fixed.”
  • “Inspect this computer’s hardware and explain what kinds of local models it can run.”

The assistant chooses steps based on the model, task, and environment. Finding a route, installing a runtime, and configuring PATH in the website animation are examples, not a mandatory pipeline for every task.

Confirm what the assistant actually did

AI Assistant can run real commands and operate on files. Tool output can tell you more than the final summary about whether installation finished, which files changed, or whether an error was resolved. After installation, return to App Desktop, refresh detection, and launch the tool to verify it.

You can stop a running task, but stopping does not undo commands already executed. Not every task prompts for confirmation at every step. Define the goal and permitted scope first, and do not casually paste unknown commands or credentials into the assistant.

Conversations and settings for each turn

Create, switch, and delete conversations to keep projects or tasks separate. Deleting a conversation requires confirmation, but does not uninstall tools that were installed during it. Settings such as the model and reasoning effort are generally determined when you send a message. A running task uses the settings submitted for that turn; later adjustments mainly affect the next turn.

Connect to an existing agent

Connect mode currently supports an installed Claude Code CLI. In this mode, Claude Code handles the turn using its own environment, tools, memory, and model configuration. EchoBird hides its model selector.

To change that model, manage it in App Desktop or Claude Code’s own settings. Do not assume that model selection in normal assistant mode applies to Connect mode.

Run tasks on your own server

Add an SSH server on the right by entering its host, port, username, and authentication details. Test the connection before selecting it for a task. The remote machine must already have an accessible SSH service; this feature does not purchase or create a cloud server for you.

Deleting a server removes only its saved connection entry, not software on the remote machine. Follow the actual prompts when system privileges are needed. Local steps that require a password may be handed over to a native terminal.

title: Local LLM
summary: Download or scan model files, prepare a runtime engine, then start your own model service.
body:
Understand model files and engines first

Local LLM manages model files, inference engines, and service processes. It is included in the full edition and controlled by the optional-page switch in Settings.

Model files contain the weights. The runtime engine loads them and provides a service. Finishing a download does not mean the service has started, and installing an engine does not mean a model has been downloaded. GGUF is a common format for local model files.

Start with your first local model

  1. In Store, review the models and hardware guidance, and choose a quantized version suited to your machine. If you already have files, add a local model directory and scan it.
  2. Choose a runtime, detect the corresponding engine, and install it. Use the available controls to select a version or upgrade when needed.
  3. Select the model, port, compute resources, and context length. Start with conservative settings, then adjust model size and context once the basic setup works.
  4. Click Start, wait for output, and check the service status, address, and access key. If it fails, read the logs first rather than repeatedly starting it.
  5. Once the service works, use it through AI Assistant or another supported model entry.
  6. Click Stop when you are done to release resources used by the service. Leaving the page does not stop the service.

Choose a runtime for your system

Runtime pathWhen it applies
llama.cppThe basic runtime path on all three platforms; performance depends on the hardware and build
macOS MetalCan use acceleration on supported Apple hardware
NVIDIA CUDARequires a supported NVIDIA environment and a corresponding build
CPUA basic option without a suitable GPU; speed depends on the model and hardware
vLLM / SGLangThe current interface offers these options only on Linux when an NVIDIA or AMD GPU is detected

Larger models and longer contexts generally need more memory. Allow room for your operating system and other work applications rather than judging requirements by the model file size alone.

Directories, models, and custom commands

Removing a scan directory only removes it from the directory list; it does not delete model files from disk. You can scan again after a download finishes.

Advanced users can set a custom engine path and launch arguments. When starting out, keep a working default setup. Do not change unfamiliar arguments, ports, and model formats all at once, or it becomes difficult to identify the cause of a failure.

Use it with AI Assistant

Confirm the local service works first, then choose an available model source in the assistant. Verify model serving and task execution separately: if a model is missing, check its files and scanning; if a connection fails, check the process, port, and key; if memory is insufficient, reduce the model size or context.

Running inference locally does not make every task offline. The assistant may still access the network when downloading dependencies, visiting web pages, or calling external services.
